summary: Strong Phase 1 artifact with a coherent Stage 4 73 surface, exact 73-key E1-E7 keybed, clean technical gates, accessible decorative controls, and a truthful generated basic piano voice. The main limitations are visual exactness at hardware/micro-label level, very compressed narrow presentation, shallow real-audio verification, and incomplete exercised status/fallback cleanup paths.

criteria.label: Silhouette, chassis, and geometry
evidence: The rendered instrument uses the Stage 4 73 aspect ratio 3.0951 and the sealed desktop capture shows one continuous red chassis with rails, front lip, end cheeks, and no marketing hero.
Runtime inspection at 1440x900 measured the instrument at 1324.8 x 428.0 px, about 92% of viewport width, with deck/keybed regions intact and no body overflow.
The keybed generation is exact for the assigned variant: tests and runtime found 73 total keys, 43 white keys, 30 black keys, E1 through E7.

criteria.label: Complete hardware inventory and placement
evidence: The artifact defines six sections in the documented order and fractions: performance, organ, piano, program, synth, and effects.
Runtime inspection found 122 data-control-id controls, 9 organ drawbars, and exactly 2 OLED elements, matching the Program/Synth-only primary OLED requirement.

Major landmarks are present in each section, but the inventory is still schematic rather than a complete reference-level recreation: many small labels/LED groupings are compressed, simplified, or represented as generic controls.

criteria.label: Materials, color, typography, and displays
evidence: Screenshots show credible red chassis material, dark inset panels, white/black key material, green LED ladders, and blue OLED treatments.
Typography and micro-detail are not reference-exact: labels are often tiny or ellipsized, display content is simplified, and many controls read as a diagrammatic approximation.

criteria.label: Narrow retention
evidence: At 390x844 runtime inspection measured a complete 374.4 x 121.0 px instrument with 43 white keys, 30 black keys, 122 controls, 2 OLEDs, and no horizontal or vertical overflow.
The narrow screenshot retains the full chassis and keybed, but the surface is extremely compressed; most control labels and detailed state are not realistically legible at that viewport.

criteria.label: Unified playable inputs
evidence: Pointer key input, pointer cancel, mapped computer keyboard input with repeat suppression, MIDI note on/off, MIDI velocity, MIDI CC64 sustain, MIDI denied, and MIDI disconnected states are implemented and covered by tests.
The App routes pointer, keyboard, and MIDI paths through the same GeneratedPianoEngine noteOn/noteOff lifecycle.
Independent touch is represented through pointerId-tracked sources, but there is no direct multitouch/browser touch regression test.

criteria.label: Voice lifecycle and performance
evidence: GeneratedPianoEngine tests cover overlapping repeated notes, per-source release, sustain hold/release, repeat suppression, deterministic voice stealing, velocity storage, and allNotesOff.
Runtime interaction confirmed a C4 pointer press updates the status to Voices 1, and decorative control movement does not change the audio status.

Released voices remain in the engine snapshot until cleanupReleased is called, and cleanupReleased is not scheduled by the app; actual Web Audio node cleanup is implemented with timeouts but not directly tested at the browser/audio boundary.

criteria.label: Basic source and status honesty
evidence: IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json truthfully declares a generated browser-synthesis voice with no recorded samples or external audio assets.
The UI status reports 'Basic piano: ready generated synthesis', which matches the implementation and does not falsely claim Nord samples or multiple piano models.
There is no exercised loading/error/fallback flow beyond the ready generated-synthesis path, despite the engine exposing fallback/error status types.

criteria.label: Control movement and feedback
evidence: Every hardware control is rendered from HARDWARE_CONTROLS with stable data-control-id, accessible name, and pointer/keyboard handlers.
Buttons expose aria-pressed; knobs, encoders, faders, drawbars, wheels, and stick expose slider roles with aria-valuenow and visible focus.
The movement model is basic: pointer down increments once, there is no drag tracking, and all non-button controls share generic slider semantics rather than control-specific interaction.

criteria.label: Decorative-control boundary
evidence: Panel controls update only local presentation state in controlState; they are not wired to the piano engine or any system state.
Control labels and titles explicitly mark panel controls as decorative in Phase 1, while keybed notes and keyboard/MIDI sustain are the only functional audio paths.
Tests and runtime interaction verified the master-level decorative knob changes aria-valuenow without altering the ready generated-piano status.

criteria.label: Data structure and tests
evidence: The source uses normalized hardware data for sections, controls, and generated keybed geometry, with stable IDs and tests mapped to all required feature IDs.
Audio behavior is separated into GeneratedPianoEngine and an injectable AudioAdapter, allowing deterministic unit tests without hardware audio output.

Test coverage is meaningful for Phase 1 basics but shallow for full fidelity: no real Web Audio/offline render assertions, no direct browser multitouch test, no exhaustive visual diff, and no scheduled released-voice cleanup assertion.

criteria.label: Runtime quality
evidence: Local reruns of pnpm run test, typecheck, lint, and build all passed; the sealed verification also records all four required checks as passed.
Playwright runtime inspection found no console messages or page errors at desktop or narrow viewport.
The app remains responsive through key and decorative-control interactions, but the status/fallback lifecycle is minimal and released voice objects can accumulate until later cleanup or stealing.

issues: Narrow 390px rendering preserves the whole instrument but compresses it to about 121px tall, making detailed controls and labels mostly illegible.
Visual inventory is dense and sectionally correct, but many hardware details are simplified into schematic generic controls rather than reference-accurate labels, LEDs, and exact placements.
Audio verification relies on stateful/null-adapter tests; it does not measure actual rendered Web Audio output or node cleanup at the browser boundary.
GeneratedPianoEngine keeps released voices in its internal snapshot until cleanupReleased or later polyphony stealing; the app does not schedule cleanupReleased.
The UI exposes a ready generated-synthesis status but does not exercise loading, error, or playable fallback states.
